input.rationale: All four registered questions now carry decided accounts with complete comparison sets, so the last useful action is to make the parent finding's measured effect durable in the same form as the other two findings: a behavior entry citing the receipts that decided it. Nothing in the accounts changes, no question is reopened and no experiment is requested; the remaining unmeasured ground (production store implementations, horizons beyond ten seconds, and the child questions' own bounds) stays recorded as limitation inside the parent interpretation.

knowledge.statement: A follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its cached last log entry never accepts another log entry from that leader: the cached claim keeps outranking the installed snapshot in getLastEntry, every prev-log check fails, the leader walks nextIndex down until it can no longer read its own trimmed log, and it re-ships the same snapshot. Measured at three and five voters and over three-, four- and ten-second windows: the follower's FSM was restored repeatedly (4 -> 1193 in three seconds, 5 -> 4788 in ten) while its applied index stayed at the snapshot index and the cluster frontier advanced (83 -> 95 in three seconds, 83 -> 123 in ten); its commit index stayed 0 and the cached claim persisted above the snapshot index. With a monotonic log store the store was emptied (first and last index 0) while the claim persisted unchanged, and publishing a snapshot above the claim (index 98 against a claim of 97) restored the follower to the frontier.
knowledge.conditions: In-process stores (InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore and its monotonic wrapper) with TrailingLogs=10 against a large-trailing control, one induced partition of a single voter that holds an uncommitted suffix from a superseded leader, its restart on the unchanged stores, an idle cluster with one client write per 250 ms sample and no automatic snapshotting, three or five voters, and the leader's snapshot index remaining at or below the follower's cached claim throughout the window.

knowledge.statement: The InstallSnapshot handler does not update the receiving node's cached last log entry (lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm). It sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot to the request's LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm, replaces the committed and latest configurations, and then either deletes the whole log store (monotonic store) or calls compactLogs, which trims only up to min(snapshotIndex, cachedLastLogIndex - TrailingLogs).
knowledge.conditions: Reached by a follower for an accepted snapshot request in the installSnapshot declaration cited as src_install_snapshot_tail (raft.go 1837-1977; the lastApplied/lastSnapshot/configuration/compaction tail at raft.go 1952-1977); compaction rules cited as src_compaction (snapshot.go 217-279); cache accessors cited as src_get_last_entry (state.go 160-174).

knowledge.statement: getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, and the snapshot's (index,term) only when the cached log index is strictly below the snapshot index. A follower whose cached log index is at or above the newly installed snapshot index therefore keeps reporting its pre-snapshot log tail as its last entry, both for prev-log verification of incoming AppendEntries and for the log-completeness test used when granting votes or pre-votes.

history.correction: Citation correction only: the recorded conditions named state.go 160-175, which exceeds the file length of 174 lines. The behavior claim is unchanged.

knowledge.statement: Leader-side repair of a rejected AppendEntries proceeds only by decrementing nextIndex (bounded below by resp.LastLog+1), and setupAppendEntries returns ErrLogNotFound as soon as nextIndex-1 falls outside the leader's trimmed log store; replicateTo then jumps to SEND_SNAP, which re-sends the newest stored snapshot and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1. Repeating this cycle converges on re-installing the same snapshot index whenever the follower's prev-log checks fail at and above that index.
knowledge.conditions: replication.go 240-300 and 352-372; requires the leader's log to have been trimmed by a snapshot (TrailingLogs smaller than the gap), which is the normal steady state after log compaction.

knowledge.statement: An identical TimeoutNow payload honoured a second time is treated exactly like a fresh one: the receiver clears its known leader, becomes a Candidate and sets the candidate-from-transfer flag, so a further election runs. In the measured three-voter history the term rose from 3 to 4 and the same node was re-elected, one leaderless sample appeared in 138 samples taken at 10 ms, and one client write out of 138 attempts, issued at the moment of the duplicate, was refused with 'node is not the leader'; the refusal window lasted less than one 10 ms step.
knowledge.conditions: Three voters with ten committed entries, in-process transport, one duplicated payload delivered through another node's transport, sampling and writes every 10 ms for 1.5 s; the transfer flag is what bypasses the known-leader vote rejection, so the effect is specific to the transfer path rather than to the request's log content.

knowledge.statement: A configuration change whose new quorum includes a server holding an uncommitted suffix beyond its installed snapshot index cannot gather acknowledgements and does not commit, and the leader then refuses further configuration requests: in the measured five-voter history, removing a phantom holder committed in 0 ms, removing a consistent follower did not commit within 5001 ms, and the follow-up removal of the phantom holder was refused with a 1000 ms enqueue timeout and did not commit within a further two seconds.
knowledge.conditions: Five voters with a shared prefix ending at 42 and an uncommitted suffix to 75-82 in the older term, the majority leader's snapshot at 63, both minority members holding a cached claim above that snapshot after installing it, and RemoveServer requests issued on the majority leader with the ordinary enqueue timeout; the leader's reported configuration size after a blocked change reflects the locally adopted latest configuration, not the committed one.

result.summary: With all four registered questions now carrying decided accounts and complete comparison sets, this final update makes the parent finding's measured effect durable in the same form as the other two findings: one behavior entry citing the four receipts that decided it. It records that a follower which accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its cached last log entry never accepts another entry from that leader — the cached claim keeps outranking the installed snapshot in getLastEntry, every prev-log check fails, the leader walks nextIndex down until it cannot read its trimmed log and re-ships the same snapshot — with the measured numbers across three and five voters and three-, four- and ten-second windows (restores 4 -> 1193 and 5 -> 4788, applied index fixed at the snapshot index while the frontier advanced 83 -> 95 and 83 -> 123, commit index 0, claim persisting), the monotonic-store variant where the store was emptied while the claim persisted, and the repair boundary where a snapshot at 98 against a claim of 97 restored the follower. Conditions, sources and execution indices are attached, so later work can reuse or correct it by revision. No account changed, no question reopened and no experiment requested; remaining unmeasured ground stays recorded as limitation in the parent interpretation (in-process store and snapshot implementations only, horizons beyond ten seconds, bounded write rate, and the child questions' own bounds).
